title: Closed support, truncation and derived limits
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda$ be admissible, meaning one of $A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, where $A$ is a finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is a finite subextension of $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\mathcal O_E$ is its ring of integers. View $A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E$ as their associated condensed rings, with the discrete topology on $A$ and the $\ell$-adic topologies on the others [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use instead the condensed ring whose sections on a profinite set $P$ are the continuous maps $P\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with image contained in some single finite subextension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ for a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Write $D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_T))$ for the unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with its standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with open complement $j:V\hookrightarrow X$, and let $u:S\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Use the coefficient-compatible inverse images $i^*,j^*,u^*$ and direct image $j_*$ [def-sfb-module-upper-star, def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. Use the kernel construction of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support], written explicitly as the additive left exact sheaf functor
$$\underline\Gamma_Z(M)=i^*\ker(M\longrightarrow j_*j^*M),$$
where the map is the unit of $j^*\dashv j_*$, and write $R\underline\Gamma_Z$ for its total right derived functor [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Then
$$R\underline\Gamma_Z:D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\longrightarrow D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda),\qquad u^*R\underline\Gamma_Z:D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\longrightarrow D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$$
are left t-exact (they carry $D^{\geq0}$ into $D^{\geq0}$) and commute with derived inverse limits of sequences [def-weil-derived-limit]. The same two conclusions hold for tensoring with a finite locally free $\Lambda_S$-module sheaf $L$: locally on the pro-étale site $L$ is isomorphic to $\Lambda_S^{\oplus r}$ for a finite integer $r\geq0$, and the functor is $L[0]\otimes_{\Lambda_S}^{\mathrm L}-$, equivalently the functor induced by ordinary termwise tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules]. Commutation with a sequential derived limit means that applying the functor to its Roos triangle yields a Roos triangle for the image sequence.

proof.text: The coefficient identification $f^{-1}\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_X$ and the resulting equality of module pullback with exact inverse image are supplied by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation] to the closed immersion $i$ and the open immersions $j,u$: these inverse images are exact and preserve small limits of module sheaves, in particular countable products. By [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction], $j_*$ is right adjoint to $j^*$; thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits] shows that it too preserves these limits. Consequently $G=\underline\Gamma_Z=i^*\ker(\mathrm{id}\to j_*j^*)$ is additive, left exact, and preserves countable products. Indeed a compatible tuple in the kernel of the product map is precisely a tuple in its component kernels; the same finite-limit computation gives left exactness. This uses no exactness assertion about $i_*$.

source.place: Tag 09AA, lemma-closed-immersion (1); open slice restriction and the module adjunction; kernel computation

proof.text: By [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] the module-sheaf categories on the fixed small pro-étale models are Grothendieck abelian. Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] to a module placed in degree zero: its degree-zero component is a monomorphism into an injective module, so these categories have enough injectives. If $K\in D^{\geq0}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] supplies a representative vanishing below zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-injective-resolution-mono] with lower bound zero, it has an injective resolution $I^\bullet$ vanishing below zero. This is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. The definition [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] computes $RG(K)$ by $G(I^\bullet)$, which still vanishes in negative degrees. This proves left t-exactness of $R\underline\Gamma_Z$.

For a countable family $(K_n)$ choose K-injective representatives $I_n$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The termwise product $I=\prod_n I_n$ is K-injective and represents $\prod_nK_n$ by [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective]. Thus [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] and step 1 give
$$R\underline\Gamma_Z(\prod_nK_n)=G(\prod_n I_n)\cong\prod_n G(I_n).$$
The last complex represents $\prod_nR\underline\Gamma_Z(K_n)$ by [det-pe-products-derived], applied on $Z$. All maps are the maps induced by product projections, so this is the product comparison itself. This proves preservation of derived countable products without assuming that a product of arbitrary underived objects already computes their derived product.

source.place: Tag 0BK6, lemma-product-K-injective; Tag 07KC, lemma-products; Injectives Tag 079P

proof.text: By step 1, $u^*$ is an exact functor of module sheaves preserving countable products. Its induced functor is termwise and triangulated by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Exactness gives $H^q(u^*C)=u^*H^q(C)$, by applying $u^*$ to the kernel, image and cokernel defining cohomology. Hence it preserves $D^{\geq0}$. By [det-pe-products-derived], termwise computation of products on both $Z$ and $S$ shows that $u^*$ preserves derived countable products. With steps 2 and 3 this gives left t-exactness and product preservation for $u^*R\underline\Gamma_Z$.

source.place: Tag 07KC, lemma-products, applied to the exact open restriction; proetale.tex Tag 09AA and open slice restriction

proof.text: The functor $T_L=L\otimes_{\Lambda_S}-$ preserves finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-finite-free-tensor-exact], since the local finite-free hypothesis here is precisely its covering hypothesis. It is also a left adjoint by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], so [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits], applied to the opposite adjunction, gives preservation of finite colimits. Thus $T_L$ is exact. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] its termwise functor on complexes is triangulated. For any complex $C$, exactness identifies $T_L(\ker d_C^q)$ with $\ker(T_Ld_C^q)$ and $T_L(\operatorname{im}d_C^{q-1})$ with $\operatorname{im}(T_Ld_C^{q-1})$. Applying $T_L$ to the quotient of these subobjects gives $H^q(T_LC)\cong T_LH^q(C)$. In particular $T_L$ takes acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes and preserves quasi-isomorphisms. For acyclic $C$, symmetry identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes L[0])$ with $T_LC$, which is acyclic. Thus $L[0]$ is K-flat by [def-pc-kflat-complex], and its terms are flat (tensor with $L$ is exact, and all other terms are zero). By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], choose for $C$ a quasi-isomorphic K-flat complex $P$ with flat terms. That node identifies $L[0]\otimes^{\mathrm L}C$ with $L\otimes P$; exactness of $T_L$ identifies the latter in the derived category with $L\otimes C$. The representative comparisons are natural and compatible with inversion of quasi-isomorphisms by that same cited statement. Hence the derived tensor is the termwise functor, and the cohomology identity proves t-exactness, in particular left t-exactness.

source.place: finite locally free tensor clause; exactness from the existing finite-limit theorem and the tensor-Hom adjunction

proof.text:
For any family of module sheaves $(M_n)$ the canonical map
$$L\otimes\prod_nM_n\longrightarrow\prod_n(L\otimes M_n)$$
is an isomorphism. To check it, restrict to every member $U$ of one cover trivializing $L$. Restriction to the localized site is the evaluation formula of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; products restrict to products, since their sections and scalar actions are coordinatewise. Tensor restricts to tensor: the presheaf tensor formula and the sheafification in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] use on an object over $U$ exactly the same covering families in the slice as in the original site. Where $L|_U\cong\Lambda_U^{\oplus r}$, the displayed map is the coordinate-reindexing isomorphism $(\prod_nM_n|_U)^{\oplus r}\cong\prod_n(M_n|_U)^{\oplus r}$ for finite $r$. These local inverses agree on overlaps, since each is inverse to the restriction of the same comparison; the sheaf gluing axiom therefore gives a global inverse. This is a local finite-coordinate calculation, including $r=0$, not a claim that local freeness implies global freeness.

source.place: tensor product clause; elementary local finite-free product calculation

proof.text: Apply [det-pe-products-derived] on $S$ to representatives of a countable family of derived objects. By step 5, tensor with $L$ is its exact termwise functor, and by step 6 it commutes with the products in each degree. It follows that $L[0]\otimes^{\mathrm L}-$ preserves countable products in $D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$. The functor $R\underline\Gamma_Z$ is triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated], applied to the additive sheaf functor $G$; its source and target have K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Step 4 and step 5 give the same triangulated property for $u^*R\underline\Gamma_Z$ and tensor with $L$.

source.place: Tag 07KC, lemma-products; right derived functors and distinguished triangles

proof.text:
Let $F$ be any of the three functors in the statement, and let $(K_n,t_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n)$ be any sequence in its source. Write its derived-limit triangle, in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit], as
$$H\longrightarrow P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\longrightarrow H[1],\qquad P=\prod_nK_n,\qquad \mathrm{pr}_ns=t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}.$$
The products exist by [det-pe-products-derived], and a derived limit exists by [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] (1). The preceding steps show that $F$ is additive and triangulated and that the canonical comparison $\phi:F(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_nF(K_n)$ is invertible. For every $n$,
$$\mathrm{pr}'_n\phi F(s)=F(\mathrm{pr}_ns)=F(t_n)F(\mathrm{pr}_{n+1})=F(t_n)\mathrm{pr}'_{n+1}\phi.$$
The product universal property gives $\phi F(s)=s'\phi$ and hence $\phi F(1-s)=(1-s')\phi$. Apply $F$ to the distinguished triangle and use $\phi$ on its two product vertices. The result is exactly a Roos triangle for the image sequence, so $F(H)$ is its derived limit. This proves the required commutation. No uniqueness or canonical choice of comparison between arbitrary triangulated-category cones is asserted.

split_report.summary: Expanded the definition of the support functor to remove the circular dependency through the constructibility preamble of sk-lem-formal-closed-support. Proved left t-exactness on bounded-below injective representatives, product preservation on K-injective products, the local finite-free tensor comparison, and the explicit Roos transition calculation. Reused existing generic nodes throughout; no new nodes. No hypotheses were added. The optional adjunction to termwise closed pushforward is not needed, so quasi-compactness of the open complement is not required. Repair of returned head 76df629bd6: refreshed the sandbox chapter/unit binding from current main and included the existing unit record with only realized and realized_by updated, so landing requires no out-of-delivery unit fix. Current main has repaired the former dependency cycle below sk-lem-formal-closed-support; restored that statement dependency for its support-kernel construction, preserving the unit route while retaining the explicit eight-step proof. Second reading corrects the algebraic-closure coefficient to the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring of sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed; the eight proof steps apply to that actual ring unchanged.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the complete main-20261015 statement and unit proof: support-kernel construction from sk-lem-formal-closed-support, exact restriction and products in steps 1–4, finite locally free tensor in steps 5–7, and the fiber-of-one-minus-shift reduction in step 8. The support dependency is restored after checking that its current-main closure no longer returns to this item. The proof computes the right derived kernel functor directly rather than using exactness of arbitrary closed pushforward.

tool_uses.why: Step 1 needs exact inverse image and small-limit preservation for module sheaves along closed and open immersions, including the coefficient-ring isomorphism. The unit gives the restriction/product route but no module-sheaf version of this geometric input.

Steps 1 and 5 use the general adjunction theorem for limits, respectively for j_* and, in opposite categories, the tensor left adjoint. The unit invokes right-adjoint preservation without stating this categorical input.
Step 2 needs the Grothendieck property of module sheaves on a small ringed site to apply the injective-resolution existence theorem; the unit has no statement of this general ringed-site fact.
Step 2 extracts enough injectives from the termwise monic K-injective resolution in a Grothendieck category. The unit supplies no injective-existence theorem.

Step 2 needs an injective resolution preserving the explicit lower bound zero to prove left t-exactness. The unit has no such bounded-resolution theorem; this implements its left-exact derived-functor argument.
Step 2 uses bounded-below injectives as K-injective representatives for the unbounded right derived functor. The unit has no statement of this generic homological-algebra criterion.

Steps 3 and 7 need K-injective resolutions for arbitrary unbounded complexes of coefficient module sheaves. This ringed-site theorem is not supplied by the unit and does not replace its product/Roos argument.
Step 3 needs the derived-product representation by products of K-injective complexes in an abelian category. The unit supplies the pro-etale product input but no general K-injective-product theorem.
Steps 4 and 5 pass exact open restriction and finite locally free tensor termwise to triangulated derived functors. The unit has no statement of this generic exact-functor construction.

Step 5 uses finite-limit preservation for tensor with an internal module trivialized by a pro-etale cover, over the actual coefficient ring sheaf. The unit asserts tensor exactness but has no separate general local-freeness input.
Step 5 needs the ordinary tensor-Hom adjunction on module sheaves over a commutative ringed site to deduce finite-colimit preservation. The unit gives no statement of this generic sheaf adjunction.
Step 7 needs triangulated exactness of the unbounded right derived additive support functor. The unit uses fibers but supplies no general right-derived triangulated theorem.

Step 8 uses only clause (1), existence of a Roos triangle when the countable product exists. The unit invokes sequential derived limits without stating this general triangulated-category existence fact.

Step 5 identifies the exact termwise tensor with the derived tensor on the actual ringed site via K-flat representatives with flat terms. The unit states tensor exactness but supplies no resolution/descent comparison.
